solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Boy is good artist and bad actor

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword stock artist
a ham is an actor who overplays badly

explanation.surface: A lad who paints well but cannot act to save his life.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common male first name, so any boy might bear it.

clue.text: A huge amount of sticky stuff: precious commodity, mostly

parts.note: goo is sticky gunk

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: gold is a precious metal traded as a commodity

explanation.surface: A vast quantity of gunk that is nearly as valuable as treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of GOLD, leaving GOL.
explanation.definitionFit: It is ten to the power of a hundred, a vast number.

clue.text: Not in favour of August, on reflection, in Caribbean location

parts.note: anti means opposed to

indicators.note: on reflection means the month's abbreviation is mirrored, read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone who, thinking it over, dislikes August in the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an island nation in the Caribbean Sea.

clue.text: Idiot grabbing first of poisonous snakes

indicators.note: grabbing means the fool's word holds the letter inside it

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of the word poisonous

explanation.surface: A fool picks up the first venomous snakes he sees.
explanation.definitionFit: Small venomous Egyptian vipers, the kind that killed Cleopatra.

clue.text: One or two, for example, less feeling

definitions.meaning: one and two are examples of a numeral
the comparative of numb: having less sensation

explanation.surface: Counting off one or two items, with a little less sensation each time.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading needs the word said as NUM-er, the comparative of numb, not the counting word.
explanation.definitionFit: One and two are integers, and an anaesthetised limb grows ever more deadened.

clue.text: Politician I call, after uniform for referee's job

indicators.note: after means the politician and the rest follow the letter for uniform

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
MP is a Member of Parliament
to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: A politician phoning after a uniformed official about refereeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Officiating a match, as in cricket or tennis, is the work a referee does.

clue.text: Fiddlestick that is used by rock star

parts.note: a bow is the stick a violinist draws over the strings
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A rock musician picks up a violin bow.
explanation.definitionFit: David of Ziggy Stardust fame was a famous rock singer.

clue.text: Try air shot: you don't often see that!

indicators.note: shot means broken or ruined, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Taking a shot into the air is something you rarely witness.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncommon or seldom seen is a curiosity.

clue.text: Envy festive, exotic figure

indicators.note: exotic means strange or unusual, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Coveting a party-season outfit on an exotic person.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure is a number, and three quarters of a hundred is one.

clue.text: Substantially increase level — put cork back, partially

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An instruction for a level surface where a cork is pushed back into a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partially' takes ELPUTCO from levEL PUT COrk, and 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To multiply eightfold is a substantial increase by any measure.

clue.text: Might war prisoner, perhaps, when meeting the queen?

parts.note: a POW is a prisoner of war
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen

explanation.surface: Asks whether a captured soldier might get to meet the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' reads as the verb 'may', but it is the noun meaning strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Might as a noun is strength or force, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Binge over, guy must purge insides

indicators.note: each of the two words loses its inner letters, keeping only the outside ones

explanation.surface: After a binge, a man needs to clean out his system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must purge insides' applies to both 'over' and 'guy': OVER keeps OR, GUY keeps GY.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild bout of excessive indulgence is a binge.

clue.text: Converted triremes: most jolly!

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ancient warships turned to new use make for the happiest outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of merry, which is a synonym of jolly.

clue.text: Van to deliver greener sort of petrol

parts.note: the van is the front, so to be in the van is to lead
to deliver someone is to set them free

explanation.surface: A delivery van that runs on more eco-friendly fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Unleaded fuel was introduced as the less polluting kind of petrol.

clue.text: Middle-Easterner, most sickly looking, at home with Scotsman?

parts.note: the palest person looks the most sickly
someone in is at home
Ian is a typical Scottish name, so stands for a Scotsman

explanation.surface: A very peaky man from the Middle East lodging with a Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the territory beside Israel is a Middle-Easterner.

clue.text: A paper, it's said, that may get someone's blessing?

indicators.note: it's said signals the words are spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: a tissue is a paper handkerchief

explanation.surface: A newspaper, so people say, that might win approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paper' looks like a newspaper but is a paper hanky; the sneeze sounds like 'a tissue'.
explanation.definitionFit: The sneeze sound draws a 'bless you' from bystanders.

clue.text: Wobble from person summing up?

definitions.meaning: one who tots, or adds up, figures

explanation.surface: A judge summarising a case begins to sway.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger is to wobble, and to tot up is to add numbers.

clue.text: Two XVs in need of a drink with seconds to go

indicators.note: to go means the letter is taken away

parts.note: thirsty means needing a drink

explanation.surface: Two rugby teams desperate for a drink with seconds left in the match.
explanation.walkthrough: XV is fifteen in Roman numerals, also a rugby union team.
explanation.definitionFit: Two times fifteen makes the number thrice ten.

clue.text: Switch positions occasionally

definitions.meaning: the two settings a light switch can be in

explanation.surface: Someone changes places every now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: A light switch has two settings, and doing something intermittently is doing it now and then.

clue.text: Intention to keep South West afloat

indicators.note: to keep means the aim word holds the compass letters inside

parts.note: an aim is an intention
SW is the abbreviation for south-west

explanation.surface: A plan to keep a region of England from going under.
explanation.definitionFit: Floating on or in water, swimming, is being afloat.

clue.text: Husband following Women's Institute's fancy

indicators.note: following means the husband's letter comes after the institute's

parts.note: WI is the Women's Institute, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A husband trails along after his wife's club's whims.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI (Women's Institute) is a British community organisation for women.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy as a noun is a desire or longing, the same as a hope.

clue.text: A lot of money understandably can help at first

indicators.note: at first means taking the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Plenty of cash, naturally, can make things easier.
explanation.definitionFit: A great quantity is a synonym for a lot.

clue.text: Person who drags loom

definitions.meaning: one who tows something, a tow-truck driver say
to loom is to rise high over something

explanation.surface: Someone who hauls a weaving machine around.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is said to rhyme with 'goer', the second with 'power'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hauler is someone who pulls things, and to loom is to rise menacingly above.

clue.text: Pained expression when cutting very short ticket

indicators.note: cutting means the exclamation slices into the trimmed word
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: ouch is what one says when hurt

explanation.surface: Someone winces at a ticket that has been trimmed far too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims VERY to VER, and 'cutting' puts OUCH into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupon or token exchangeable for goods is a kind of ticket.

clue.text: Hammers backing you to become England football manager

parts.note: rams as a verb means hammers or strikes hard

indicators.note: backing means the old word for you is read in reverse

parts.note: ye is an old word for you

explanation.surface: West Ham (nicknamed the Hammers) supporting you until you're running England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns YE into EY. Sir Alf Ramsey managed England to their 1966 World Cup win; the Hammers is West Ham United's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Alf managed the England team that won the 1966 World Cup.

clue.text: Conservative pinching man's idea

indicators.note: pinching means the party word grips the pronoun inside it

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
he stands for a man

explanation.surface: A Tory politician steals another man's idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypothesis or supposition is an idea someone puts forward.
